$comment: Per-route first-load JS budgets, in KB gzipped. Enforced by
scripts/bundle-budget.mts, which runs in CI and fails the build.
── The spec's number, and why these are not it ──
See ADR-010. PHASE-03-KUNDLI-UI.md §7 asks for < 180 KB gzipped on
the kundli route. Measured 2026-09-19, that route is 201.0 KB and
the floor under it — React, react-dom and the Next client runtime,
before a single line of this product — is 159.5 KB. Two chunks
account for 112 KB of that and contain no product code at all.
So 180 KB leaves about 20 KB for everything Ayana does, and the
i18n dictionaries alone are 14.8 KB. Measured, not estimated:
deleting the glossary prose (8.9 KB) AND the entire Hindi
dictionary (7.1 KB) — every removable byte — lands at 183.0 KB.
ADR-010 therefore replaces 180 KB as the GATE criterion with the
regression budgets below. The spec number stays as specTargetKB,
is printed on every run, and is recorded in PROJECT_STATUS.md as an
unmet spec item rather than quietly redefined — a target silently
moved to whatever was achieved hides the gap; an unmet one stated
plainly keeps it visible for whoever revisits the framework.
── What these budgets ARE for ──
Catching regressions. Each is the measured size plus a small
allowance, so an import that drags in a date library or a second
copy of a corpus fails the build on the PR that adds it — which is
the thing a CI budget can actually deliver.
Lowering a number here is always allowed. Raising one is a decision
that should appear in a diff with a reason next to it.
